1) Disseminated Talaromyces (Penicillium) marneffei infection
   - Why: Endemic region (southern China), chronic cough, intermittent fevers, multiple chronic cutaneous lesions/abscesses — classic pattern for disseminated penicilliosis.
   - Next confirmatory tests: HIV test; skin-lesion biopsy with fungal histopathology and culture; blood fungal culture; sputum fungal culture/PCR.

2) Disseminated nocardiosis
   - Why: Chronic pulmonary symptoms + multiple skin abscesses and intermittent fevers favor Nocardia (filamentous branching bacteria) disseminated disease.
   - Next confirmatory tests: Skin lesion aspiration/biopsy for Gram stain, modified acid-fast stain and culture (prolonged); sputum culture with Nocardia-specific requests; blood cultures if febrile.

3) Extrapulmonary/disseminated tuberculosis with cutaneous involvement
   - Why: Chronic cough and systemic symptoms in endemic area; TB can produce cutaneous lesions (scrofuloderma, lupus vulgaris) or disseminated disease even with a normal chest x-ray.
   - Next confirmatory tests: Sputum AFB smear and mycobacterial culture x3; skin biopsy for AFB & mycobacterial culture; TB PCR (GeneXpert) if available.

4) Sporotrichosis (Sporothrix schenckii complex)
   - Why: Rural, soil/gardening exposure and chronic nodular/abscessing skin lesions following inoculation/lymphatic spread; pulmonary form is rare but possible.
   - Next confirmatory tests: Skin lesion fungal culture and histopathology; culture incubated at different temperatures (dimorphic fungus).

5) Disseminated non-tuberculous mycobacterial (NTM) infection or other deep fungal infection (e.g., histoplasmosis)
   - Why: Chronic systemic symptoms with skin and possible pulmonary involvement; NTM and some endemic fungi can present similarly in rural settings.
   - Next confirmatory tests: Skin and sputum mycobacterial cultures with species identification; fungal serology/PCR and cultures as indicated.

Overall immediate priorities: HIV test, targeted sampling of skin lesions (biopsy/aspiration) for histology, bacterial/mycobacterial and fungal cultures, and sputum AFB/fungal studies — these will best distinguish the above possibilities.
